findings.headline: Your overdraft fee is above the market range.
findings.body: At $35, it is $3 above the $32 peer median and the 93rd percentile of 15 peers (middle half of the market: $30–$33.50). Overdraft pricing is the first line examiners, consumer advocates and comparison sites read.

findings.headline: Smaller premiums elsewhere on the schedule.
findings.body: Your deposited-item return fee ($12 vs a $10 median, n=22) and your outgoing domestic wire fee ($35 vs a $25 median, n=10) also sit above the peer 75th percentile. Individually modest, together they shape how the schedule reads in a side-by-side comparison.

findings.stat_label: comparable lines inside the market range
findings.headline: Most of your schedule is priced with the market.
findings.body: Of the 8 fee lines where we found both your published amount and at least eight comparable peers, four sit between the peer 25th and 75th percentiles, three above and one below.

exec_narrative: Hanmi Bank is compared with 68 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in California have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 8 rankable lines, four sit inside the middle half of the market, three above it (overdraft fee, deposited-item return fee and outgoing domestic wire fee), and one below it (outgoing international wire fee). We would suggest one step: review the overdraft fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $32 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Overdraft fee — $35
callouts.stat: Peer median $32 · middle half $30–$33.50 · range $10–$36 · 93rd percentile · n=15
callouts.body: Published as “Overdraft Fee - Debit Card Transaction.” At $35 it is $3 above the $32 peer median. Overdraft pricing is the first line examiners, consumer advocates and comparison sites read. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $32 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Deposited-item return fee — $12
callouts.stat: Peer median $10 · middle half $8–$10 · range $5–$20 · 95th percentile · n=22
callouts.body: Published as “Returned Deposit Item - Check or ACH.” At $12 it is $2 above the $10 peer median. This fee falls on the depositor for a check someone else wrote, which makes it a frequent example in fee-fairness criticism. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $10 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing domestic wire fee — $35
callouts.stat: Peer median $25 · middle half $21.25–$28.75 · range $15–$35 · 100th percentile · n=10
callouts.body: Published as “Outgoing Wire - Fax Request.” At $35 it is $10 above the $25 peer median. Wire fees fall mostly on business and higher-balance customers, the relationships most likely to compare institutions. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $25 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing international wire fee — $30
callouts.stat: Peer median $50 · middle half $40–$50 · 0th percentile · n=9
callouts.body: Published as “Outgoing Wire - International/Domestic/Reverse.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $50 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Hanmi Bank with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
